hannah.name: Hannah
hannah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hannah.importance: She has no children, and Peninnah provokes her each year at Shiloh. She weeps, prays, and vows to give a son to the LORD. Samuel is born, and she brings him to Eli once he is weaned. Then she prays a song of praise.
hannah.connections: Wife of Elkanah. Mother of Samuel, then of three more sons and two daughters.

peninnah.name: Peninnah
peninnah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
peninnah.importance: She has children, and Hannah has none. Year after year she provokes Hannah on the trip to Shiloh. Hannah weeps and does not eat. The book does not name Peninnah after chapter 1.
peninnah.connections: Elkanah’s wife beside Hannah. She has sons and daughters.

elkanah.name: Elkanah
elkanah.role: Husband who takes his family to Shiloh
elkanah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
elkanah.importance: He takes his family to Shiloh each year to worship and sacrifice. He gives Hannah a double portion and asks why she weeps. He agrees that she may keep Samuel home until he is weaned. Eli blesses him and Hannah in chapter 2.
elkanah.connections: Husband of Hannah and Peninnah. Father of Samuel.

samuel.name: Samuel
samuel.role: Prophet and judge who anoints kings
samuel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
samuel.importance: As a boy he hears the LORD call and tells Eli the hard message. He judges Israel, prays at Mizpah, and warns the people about a king. He anoints Saul, later tells him the LORD has rejected him, and anoints David. He dies in chapter 25, yet Saul asks for him at Endor.
samuel.connections: Son of Hannah and Elkanah. Father of Joel and Abijah.

eli.name: Eli
eli.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
eli.importance: He thinks Hannah is drunk, then blesses her prayer. He scolds his sons but does not stop them. He teaches Samuel how to answer the LORD’s call. He falls and dies when he hears the ark is taken.
eli.connections: Father of Hophni and Phinehas. He raises the boy Samuel at Shiloh.

hophni.name: Hophni
hophni.role: Eli’s son and priest at Shiloh
hophni.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
hophni.importance: He and Phinehas have their servant take meat from offerings by force. They sleep with the women who serve at the Tent of Meeting. They do not listen to Eli. Both die on the day the Philistines take the ark.
hophni.connections: Son of Eli and brother of Phinehas.

phinehas-eli.name: Phinehas
phinehas-eli.role: Eli’s son and priest at Shiloh
phinehas-eli.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
phinehas-eli.importance: He is not Aaron’s grandson of the same name. He and Hophni take offerings by force and do not listen to Eli. Both die on the day the ark is taken. His wife gives birth that day and dies.
phinehas-eli.connections: Son of Eli and brother of Hophni. Father of Ichabod. Chapter 14 names Ahitub as Ichabod’s brother.

man-of-god.name: The unnamed man of God
man-of-god.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
man-of-god.importance: He comes to Eli with a message from the LORD. He says Eli honors his sons above the LORD. He says Hophni and Phinehas will die in one day as a sign. He says the LORD will raise up a faithful priest.
man-of-god.connections: He speaks to Eli about Eli’s house and its priests.

ichabod.name: Ichabod
ichabod.role: Child born the day the ark is taken
ichabod.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ichabod.importance: He is born as his mother hears that the ark is taken. She names him Ichabod and says, “The glory has departed from Israel!” She dies about that time. Chapter 14 names him only as the brother of Ahitub.
ichabod.connections: Son of Phinehas and his unnamed wife. Grandson of Eli.

ichabod-mother.name: Ichabod’s mother
ichabod-mother.role: Unnamed woman who dies after giving birth
ichabod-mother.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ichabod-mother.importance: She hears that the ark is taken and that Eli and Phinehas are dead. Her pains come, and she gives birth to a son. She names him Ichabod and says the glory has departed from Israel. She dies about that time.
ichabod-mother.connections: Wife of Phinehas and daughter-in-law of Eli.

joshua-beth-shemesh.name: Joshua
joshua-beth-shemesh.role: Man of Beth Shemesh who owns the field
joshua-beth-shemesh.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joshua-beth-shemesh.importance: He is not the Joshua who followed Moses. The cart with the ark stops in his field by a great stone. The people offer the cows there. The text tells nothing more about him.
joshua-beth-shemesh.connections: The cart with the ark stops in his field.

abinadab-ark.name: Abinadab
abinadab-ark.role: Man whose house keeps the ark
abinadab-ark.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abinadab-ark.importance: The men of Kiriath Jearim bring the ark to his house on the hill. They set apart his son Eleazar to keep it. The ark stays twenty years. He is not David’s brother or Saul’s son of the same name.
abinadab-ark.connections: Father of Eleazar, who is set apart to keep the ark.

eleazar-ark.name: Eleazar
eleazar-ark.role: Man set apart to keep the ark
eleazar-ark.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
eleazar-ark.importance: He is not Aaron’s son Eleazar. The men of Kiriath Jearim set him apart to keep the ark. The ark stays in his father’s house on the hill. The text says nothing more about him.
eleazar-ark.connections: Son of Abinadab at Kiriath Jearim.

joel-samuel.name: Joel
joel-samuel.role: Samuel’s son, a judge who takes bribes
joel-samuel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
joel-samuel.importance: Samuel makes him a judge in Beersheba with his brother Abijah. The two take bribes and twist justice. The elders point to them when they ask Samuel for a king.
joel-samuel.connections: Samuel’s firstborn son. Brother of Abijah.

abijah-samuel.name: Abijah
abijah-samuel.role: Samuel’s son, a judge who takes bribes
abijah-samuel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abijah-samuel.importance: Samuel makes him a judge in Beersheba with his brother Joel. The two take bribes and twist justice. The elders point to them when they ask for a king. He is not a king or priest named Abijah.
abijah-samuel.connections: Samuel’s second son. Brother of Joel.

saul.name: Saul
saul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
saul.importance: Samuel anoints him, and he rescues Jabesh Gilead. He offers at Gilgal and spares Agag, and Samuel says the LORD rejects him. He hunts David and has the priests of Nob killed. He falls on his sword at Mount Gilboa.
saul.connections: Son of Kish. Father of Jonathan, Merab, Michal, and other children.

kish.name: Kish
kish.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
kish.importance: His donkeys are lost, and he sends Saul and a servant to find them. The search brings Saul to Samuel. Samuel says Kish has stopped caring about the donkeys and worries for Saul.
kish.connections: A man of Benjamin, son of Abiel. Father of Saul.

saul-servant.name: Saul’s searching companion
saul-servant.role: Unnamed servant who says to ask the seer
saul-servant.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
saul-servant.importance: He and Saul search for the donkeys and do not find them. Saul wants to go home. The servant says a man of God is in the city. He offers his own silver as the gift, and they meet Samuel.
saul-servant.connections: He goes with Saul to look for Kish’s donkeys.

nahash.name: Nahash
nahash.role: Ammonite king who camps against Jabesh Gilead
nahash.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nahash.importance: He camps against Jabesh Gilead and demands every right eye for a covenant. The elders get seven days and send for help. Saul comes and strikes the Ammonites. Samuel later says his attack made the people ask for a king.
nahash.connections: Enemy of Jabesh Gilead. Saul’s army scatters his men.

jonathan-saul.name: Jonathan
jonathan-saul.role: Saul’s son, fighter, and David’s sworn friend
jonathan-saul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-saul.importance: He attacks a Philistine garrison with only his armor bearer, and Israel wins. He makes a covenant with David and gives him his robe and sword. He warns David that Saul means to kill him. He dies with Saul at Mount Gilboa.
jonathan-saul.connections: Son of Saul. Brother of Merab and Michal. He makes a covenant with David.

jonathan-armor-bearer.name: Jonathan’s armor bearer
jonathan-armor-bearer.role: Unnamed young man who climbs with Jonathan
jonathan-armor-bearer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-armor-bearer.importance: Jonathan asks him to cross to the Philistine garrison. He says he is with Jonathan. He climbs up after Jonathan and kills the men Jonathan strikes down. The two kill about twenty men, and the Philistine camp trembles.
jonathan-armor-bearer.connections: He goes with Jonathan, and Saul does not know.

ahijah-priest.name: Ahijah
ahijah-priest.role: Priest who wears an ephod with Saul
ahijah-priest.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahijah-priest.importance: He is with Saul’s six hundred men at Gibeah and wears an ephod. Saul tells him to bring God’s ark. The noise in the Philistine camp grows, and Saul tells him to stop.
ahijah-priest.connections: Son of Ahitub and grandson of Phinehas, from Eli’s house.

abner.name: Abner
abner.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abner.importance: He cannot tell Saul whose son David is, and he brings David in. He sits by Saul at the new moon meal. In chapter 26 he sleeps while David takes Saul’s spear. David calls out and blames him for not guarding the king.
abner.connections: Son of Ner. Ner and Saul’s father Kish are both sons of Abiel.

ahinoam-saul.name: Ahinoam
ahinoam-saul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahinoam-saul.importance: Chapter 14 names her as Saul’s wife and the daughter of Ahimaaz. She has no story in the book. She is not David’s wife Ahinoam of Jezreel.

merab.name: Merab
merab.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
merab.importance: Saul offers her to David if David will fight the Philistines. Saul hopes the Philistines will kill him. When the time comes, Saul gives her to Adriel. The text records no words from her.
merab.connections: Saul’s firstborn daughter and Michal’s sister. She is given to Adriel as wife.

michal.name: Michal
michal.role: Saul’s daughter who helps David escape
michal.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
michal.importance: She loves David, and Saul uses that to set a trap for him. She becomes David’s wife. She lets David down through a window and lays the teraphim in his bed. Saul later gives her to Palti.
michal.connections: Saul’s younger daughter. Wife of David, later given by Saul to Palti.

ishvi.name: Ishvi
ishvi.role: Son named in the list of Saul’s family
ishvi.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ishvi.importance: Chapter 14 lists him as a son of Saul with Jonathan and Malchishua. He has no story in the book. Chapter 31 names Abinadab with those two brothers and does not name Ishvi.

malchishua.name: Malchishua
malchishua.role: Saul’s son who dies at Gilboa
malchishua.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
malchishua.importance: Chapter 14 lists him as a son of Saul. The Philistines kill him with Jonathan and Abinadab at Mount Gilboa. The men of Jabesh Gilead take the sons’ bodies from the wall. They bury the bones.
malchishua.connections: Son of Saul. Brother of Jonathan, and of Abinadab in chapter 31.

agag.name: Agag
agag.role: Amalekite king Saul spares and Samuel kills
agag.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
agag.importance: Saul takes him alive and spares him, against the LORD’s command. Samuel calls for him at Gilgal. Agag comes cheerfully and says the bitterness of death is past. Samuel cuts him in pieces before the LORD.
agag.connections: Saul’s captive after the attack on Amalek.

eliab-david.name: Eliab
eliab-david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
eliab-david.importance: Samuel sees him first and thinks he is the LORD’s anointed. The LORD says not to look at his height. He follows Saul to battle and angrily says David came only to watch. He is not the tribal leader Eliab in Numbers.

abinadab-david.name: Abinadab
abinadab-david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abinadab-david.importance: Jesse has him pass before Samuel, and the LORD does not choose him. He follows Saul to the battle with Eliab and Shammah. He is not the ark’s host or Saul’s son of the same name.
abinadab-david.connections: Brother of David, Eliab, and Shammah.

shammah.name: Shammah
shammah.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
shammah.importance: Jesse has him pass before Samuel, and the LORD does not choose him. He follows Saul to the battle with Eliab and Abinadab.
shammah.connections: Brother of David, Eliab, and Abinadab.

goliath.name: Goliath
goliath.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
goliath.importance: He stands before Israel for forty days and calls for one man to fight. Saul and all Israel are afraid. David hits him in the forehead with a sling stone and cuts off his head. Later Ahimelech gives David his sword at Nob.
goliath.connections: A Philistine from Gath. David fights him alone.

adriel.name: Adriel
adriel.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
adriel.importance: Saul gives him Merab at the time she should have gone to David. The book says nothing more about him.
adriel.connections: Called the Meholathite. Husband of Merab.

jonathan-boy.name: Jonathan’s young attendant
jonathan-boy.role: Unnamed boy who fetches Jonathan’s arrows
jonathan-boy.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jonathan-boy.importance: Jonathan shoots arrows and sends him to find them. Jonathan calls, “Isn’t the arrow beyond you?” That call tells David to flee. The boy knows nothing of the plan and carries the weapons to the city.
jonathan-boy.connections: He serves Jonathan and carries his weapons.

ahimelech-priest.name: Ahimelech
ahimelech-priest.role: Priest at Nob who helps David
ahimelech-priest.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahimelech-priest.importance: He trembles when David comes alone. He gives David holy bread and the sword of Goliath. Doeg reports it, and Saul has him and his father’s house killed. He is not Ahimelech the Hittite in chapter 26.
ahimelech-priest.connections: Son of Ahitub. Father of Abiathar.

doeg.name: Doeg
doeg.role: Saul’s Edomite herdsman who kills the priests
doeg.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
doeg.importance: He is at Nob the day Ahimelech helps David. He tells Saul what he saw. Saul’s guards will not strike the priests, so Doeg does. He kills eighty-five priests and strikes the city of Nob.
doeg.connections: An Edomite, called the best of Saul’s herdsmen.

achish.name: Achish
achish.role: King of Gath who hosts David
achish.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
achish.importance: David first comes to him in fear and acts insane before him. Later he takes in David and six hundred men and gives him Ziklag. He believes David’s false reports about the raids. His princes distrust David, so he sends David back before the battle.
achish.connections: Son of Maoch. He gives David the town of Ziklag.

gad.name: Gad
gad.role: Prophet who tells David to leave the stronghold
gad.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
gad.importance: He tells David not to stay in the stronghold and to go to Judah. David leaves and comes to the forest of Hereth. He is not Jacob’s son Gad or the tribe of Gad.
gad.connections: He speaks to David while David is in the stronghold.

abiathar.name: Abiathar
abiathar.role: Priest who escapes the killing at Nob
abiathar.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abiathar.importance: He escapes when Doeg kills the priests and flees to David. He tells David what Saul did, and David says to stay with him. He brings the ephod when David asks the LORD about Keilah. He brings it again at Ziklag.
abiathar.connections: Son of Ahimelech. He joins David and brings an ephod.

abigail.name: Abigail
abigail.role: Woman who stops David’s attack on Nabal
abigail.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abigail.importance: A servant tells her that Nabal insulted David’s men. She loads food on donkeys, meets David, and asks him not to shed blood. David turns back, and after Nabal dies she becomes his wife. The Amalekites take her from Ziklag, and David rescues her.
abigail.connections: Wife of Nabal, then wife of David.

nabal.name: Nabal
nabal.role: Rich flock owner who refuses David’s request
nabal.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
nabal.importance: David’s men protect his shepherds, then ask for food at shearing time. He insults them and gives nothing. David sets out to kill every male in his house, and Abigail stops him. Nabal hears of it, becomes like a stone, and dies about ten days later.
nabal.connections: Husband of Abigail. He is of the house of Caleb.

ahinoam-david.name: Ahinoam
ahinoam-david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahinoam-david.importance: David takes her as wife in chapter 25. She lives with him at Gath and then at Ziklag. The Amalekites carry her off, and David rescues her. She is not Saul’s wife Ahinoam.
ahinoam-david.connections: Wife of David, named with Abigail. She is from Jezreel.

palti.name: Palti
palti.role: Man to whom Saul gives Michal
palti.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
palti.importance: Saul gives him Michal, though she is David’s wife. The text gives no reason and no words from Palti or Michal.

abishai.name: Abishai
abishai.role: David’s companion who goes into Saul’s camp
abishai.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abishai.importance: He offers to go down with David into Saul’s camp at night. He asks to pin the sleeping Saul to the ground with one stroke. David says no one may strike the LORD’s anointed. They take Saul’s spear and water jar and leave.
abishai.connections: Son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab.

ahimelech-hittite.name: Ahimelech
ahimelech-hittite.role: Hittite man David asks about the camp visit
ahimelech-hittite.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
ahimelech-hittite.importance: David asks him and Abishai who will go down to Saul’s camp. Abishai answers, and the text gives no answer from Ahimelech. He is not the priest Ahimelech of Nob.
ahimelech-hittite.connections: Named with Abishai before the camp visit.

endor-medium.name: The woman at Endor
endor-medium.role: Unnamed woman Saul asks to bring up Samuel
endor-medium.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
endor-medium.importance: Saul comes at night and asks her to bring up Samuel. She fears a trap, because Saul drove such people from the land. She cries out when she sees Samuel and knows her guest is Saul. Afterward she urges Saul to eat and cooks a calf and bread.
endor-medium.connections: Saul comes to her in disguise. She later feeds him and his servants.

egyptian-servant.name: The Egyptian servant
egyptian-servant.role: Sick Egyptian left behind who guides David
egyptian-servant.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
egyptian-servant.importance: His Amalekite master leaves him sick in the field for three days. David’s men give him bread, water, figs, and raisins. He makes David swear not to kill him or hand him back. Then he leads David to the Amalekite camp.
egyptian-servant.connections: Servant of an Amalekite who raided Ziklag.

word.languageNote: This is the dictionary form of the name “Egyptian.”

abinadab-saul.name: Abinadab
abinadab-saul.role: Saul’s son who dies at Gilboa
abinadab-saul.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
abinadab-saul.importance: The Philistines kill him with Jonathan and Malchishua at Mount Gilboa. Chapter 14 does not list him among Saul’s sons. He is not David’s brother or the ark’s host.

saul-armor-bearer.name: Saul’s armor bearer
saul-armor-bearer.role: Unnamed armor bearer at Saul’s last battle
saul-armor-bearer.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
saul-armor-bearer.importance: The archers press Saul, and he asks his armor bearer to kill him. He is terrified and will not. Saul falls on his own sword, and the armor bearer does the same. He is not Jonathan’s armor bearer from chapter 14.

jesse.name: Jesse
jesse.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
jesse.importance: He has seven sons pass before Samuel, then sends for David from the sheep. He sends David to Saul with bread, wine, and a young goat. Later he sends David to the battle with food for his brothers. David takes him to the king of Moab for safety.
jesse.connections: Father of David and seven other sons, among them Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah.

david.name: David
david.role: Shepherd anointed king who flees from Saul
david.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
david.importance: Samuel anoints him, and he plays the harp for Saul and kills Goliath. Saul tries to kill him, so he flees and gathers about six hundred men. Twice he spares Saul’s life. He lives under Achish, raids nearby peoples, leaves no one alive, and lies about it.
david.connections: Son of Jesse. Sworn friend of Jonathan. Husband of Michal, Abigail, and Ahinoam.

moses.name: Moses
moses.role: Prophet who leads Israel from Egypt
moses.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
moses.importance: Samuel says the LORD appointed Moses and Aaron. He says the LORD sent them to bring Israel’s fathers out of Egypt. Samuel uses this to show what the LORD has done for the people.
moses.connections: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Brother of Aaron and Miriam. Husband of Zipporah.

aaron.name: Aaron
aaron.life: Birth and death years are not securely known.
aaron.importance: Samuel names him with Moses in chapter 12. He says the LORD sent the two to bring Israel’s fathers out of Egypt. Aaron has no other part in this book.
aaron.connections: Son of Amram and Jochebed. Father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

gideon.name: Gideon
gideon.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
gideon.importance: Samuel lists Jerubbaal among the men the LORD sent to rescue Israel. Jerubbaal is another name for Gideon. He has no other part in this book.
gideon.connections: Son of Joash and father of Abimelech and Jotham.

jephthah.name: Jephthah
jephthah.role: Rescuer Samuel names in his speech
jephthah.life: Historical birth and death years are not securely known.
jephthah.importance: Samuel lists him among the men the LORD sent to rescue Israel. Samuel says the LORD was already their king then. Jephthah has no other part in this book.
jephthah.connections: Son of Gilead and a woman described as a prostitute. Father of one daughter.
